v4.9.079 - the page stays where you put it (#363)

#363 Roman: "when taking a photo in 3x2 the fullscreen returns to that frame and
     pushes/scrolls the frame to the middle... also in the strip views. Also when
     I draw to the pictures, then they jump/scroll to the middle."

     Not the photo. Not the drawing. Not the sync either, which is where I looked
     twice and "fixed" twice while the page kept moving by exactly the same 119
     pixels.

     Emptying a column to rebuild it throws the scroll position away, and nothing
     put it back. Every redraw of 3x2 dropped the page by about a card. A photo
     causes a redraw, so it looked as though the photo did it.

     The redraw now writes down where everything was before it empties anything,
     and puts it back afterwards - repeatedly, as the layout settles, because the
     cards do not have their final heights at first and the browser quietly
     clamps the position to whatever the page can hold at that instant. It stops
     the moment the person scrolls themselves, so it can never fight them.

     And the pull no longer touches the page position at all. It used to put you
     "back" by CENTRING the frame nearest the middle - which moved the page every
     single time, even though the code carefully measured where the frame really
     was and then threw that measurement away. A redraw that keeps your place
     needs no help; two mechanisms only fought each other.

HOW IT WAS ACTUALLY FOUND, after three wrong theories

  - the test was made to measure at TWO moments, before and after the local
    redraw. 616, then 471, with no sync involved: that killed the sync theory
  - the app was made to SAY OUT LOUD who moves the page and from where, the same
    way it already says who changes the view
  - and the test was made to name what it was measuring, which answered "html" -
    the window scrolls, not the columns, so my first fix had been faithfully
    restoring columns that never scroll

Roman asked, twice and fairly, whether I was guessing. The first three attempts
were. This one is measured.

ALSO

A test that swipes across a picture is written but not running: WebKit will not
let a test build a touch out of nothing, and the cross-swipe listens for touches
only. The rule is right and it is left in the file for the day we can drive a
real finger.

22 of 23 pass. The one failure is the random day, which disagrees on two
different seeds in the same way after one device is away while the other
rearranges. Repeatable, older than any of this. Still the next hunt.
